| Log Category | Description | Examples | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OS Logs** | Logs generated by operating systems to track system activity, events, errors, and resource usage. | Linux syslog, Windows Event Logs, kernel logs, system boot logs, authentication logs, audit logs | Troubleshooting OS issues, monitoring system health, security monitoring, and auditing. |
| **Network Logs** | Logs generated by network devices and services to capture network traffic, connectivity, and security events. | Firewall, router, switch, DNS, DHCP, VPN, load balancer, proxy, and NetFlow logs | Network troubleshooting, traffic analysis, connectivity monitoring, and threat detection. |
| **Platform Logs** | Logs generated by infrastructure platforms, virtualization environments, and container orchestration systems. | Kubernetes, VMware ESXi/vCenter, Docker, OpenStack, and cloud infrastructure platform logs | Infrastructure monitoring, deployment troubleshooting, and platform failure investigation. |
| **Middleware Logs** | Logs generated by databases, web servers, application servers, messaging platforms, and intermediate services. | Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Nginx, Apache, Tomcat, JBoss, Kafka, RabbitMQ, and cloud service logs | Service availability, database performance, transaction failures, and dependency troubleshooting. |
| **Application Logs** | Logs generated by business applications, application code, APIs, and runtime environments. | Application error/debug logs, API logs, Java, PHP, Python, business transaction, and application audit logs | Application debugging, transaction tracing, performance monitoring, and functional issue investigation. |
